What makes dragonflies so amazing?

The dragonfly, which flies freely through the sky, is an amazing flying insect. With its big eyes it can see in almost every direction at once.

content.alt: Dragonfly - Nature and science facts about dragonflies
content.text:
Nature and science facts about dragonflies

With enormous compound eyes that take up most of its head, a dragonfly can see in almost every direction at once. By moving its four wings separately, it can hover in place or even fly backward. It's helpful to people because it catches mosquitoes and flies right out of the air. Amazingly, a dragonfly's young stage (the larva, or "nymph") lives underwater; once grown, it crawls out of the water, sheds its skin, spreads its wings, and becomes an adult dragonfly.

Great points to observe together

Point out things like the big compound eyes (all-around vision), the four wings (hovering and backward flight), the underwater larva, and shedding its skin. Talking about "Isn't it amazing that dragonfly larvae live underwater?" together is a great idea.

Parent guide — how to nurture curiosity

Watch a dragonfly hover in the air near a pond or the water's edge. Tell your child "It used to live underwater when it was young," and looking at its big eyes through a magnifying glass makes it even more fun.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How does a dragonfly hover in the air?
A. Because it moves its four wings separately. That's how it can stop in place or even fly backward.

Q. Where do dragonfly larvae live?
A. Amazingly, they live underwater. Once grown, they crawl out of the water, shed their skin, and become adult dragonflies.

Q. How can we observe them at home?
A. Watch their hovering flight at a pond and look at their big compound eyes through a magnifying glass.
